subject: On-prem VPC: control/data coexistence and ops handoff
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Park <kevin@rackops.io>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem VPC: control/data coexistence and ops handoff

Hi Kevin / Marta,

Thanks for agreeing to review the on-prem VPC plan with us. ACME's infra team asked for a concise readout focused on how our control-plane traffic and inference data-plane coexist on the same physical fabric, and what ops handoff will look like during cutover.

High-level asks from ACME we want to address in this thread:
- Which subnets/VRFs are used for control-plane vs data-plane, and where egress originates.
- How KV-cache/control state traffic is routed (NAT/peering expectations).
- Minimal runbook actions for the NOC during an SLA breach / rollback.

I've attached an initial sketch (vpc-coexistence-sketch-v1.pdf) and a short ops checklist draft (ops-handoff-checklist-v1.md). Can you review the sketch and call out any requirements ACME has for NAT or inspection points?

Proposed next step: 30m sync tomorrow to walk the diagram and pin responsibilities. If that works I can send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Kevin Park <kevin@rackops.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC: control/data coexistence and ops handoff

Priya — thanks for the sketch and checklist. A few quick items from our side after a first pass: 

1) Egress & source NAT: ACME's edge policy requires that any control-plane egress to Redwood's control plane must originate from a dedicated management CIDR and be source-NATed to a short-lived mgmt IP. Is that something your control plane can present?

2) KV cache traffic: We assume peerings will allow TCP flows on 11211/6379 (we use a proxy) and that you will accept connections only from the tenant data-plane subnets. Please confirm port/ACLs.

3) Observability: our NOC requires that the first 72 hours after cutover we have an events feed (syslog/snare) to our SIEM and a lower threshold alert for token-cache pressure. Can Redwood push a basic event stream?

If you can answer those 3 items and send an updated diagram with the mgmt CIDR and where NAT will be applied, we can confirm our preflight checklist.

On calendar: Friday 09/17 10:00am PT works for us.

—Kevin
Kevin Park
Head of Integrations, RackOps (ACME partner)
kevin@rackops.io

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Park <kevin@rackops.io>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC: control/data coexistence and ops handoff

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 11:02 AM Kevin Park <kevin@rackops.io> wrote:
> Priya — thanks for the sketch and checklist. A few quick items from our side after a first pass: 
>
> 1) Egress & source NAT: ACME's edge policy requires that any control-plane egress to Redwood's control plane must originate from a dedicated management CIDR and be source-NATed to a short-lived mgmt IP. Is that something your control plane can present?

Kevin — short answers here and I'll follow with a marked-up diagram.

1) Yes. Our private control-plane agent can be pinned to a management NIC and we support SNAT at the edge (we expect ACME to advertise a small mgmt /28 to the border NAT). We will document the expected source IPs in the cutover evidence pack.

2) KV cache traffic: we use an internal proxy that speaks on configurable ports (defaults: 26379 for sentinel, 12000 for proxy). We can restrict listener bindings to the tenant data-plane CIDRs and require mTLS within the fabric. If ACME prefers specific port numbers (you mentioned 11211/6379), we can configure the proxy to accept those and translate locally.

3) Observability: Redwood can stream a condensed syslog JSON feed (TLS to your SIEM endpoint) and we can emit a token-cache pressure metric to your monitoring endpoint. We'll need a reachable collector URL and a short cert exchange for TLS.

Attached: runbook excerpt (ops-handoff-checklist-v1.md) + quick markup (vpc-coexistence-sketch-v1.pdf) with NAT/management CIDR annotated.

Next steps: I'll upload the marked diagram to the drive link Priya included and push a preflight checklist with explicit IPs once ACME confirms the mgmt /28.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Staff Engineer, Platform Services — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachment: ops-handoff-checklist-v1.md (attachment: markdown runbook excerpt)
Attachment: vpc-coexistence-sketch-v1.pdf (attachment: annotated diagram)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Park <kevin@rackops.io>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC: control/data coexistence and ops handoff

Thanks for the clarifications, Priyom and Kevin. A couple of operational clarifications from the ops playbook side: 

- Rollback trigger: if token-cache latency > 300ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets and error rate > 2% for 5 minutes, run rollback step A2 in the checklist (we will revert routing and demote new listeners).
- Maintenance window: we recommend a low-risk cutover window (2 hours) followed by a 72-hour enhanced monitoring period. During that period our NOC will keep a lower alert threshold and ACME NOC will receive the condensed syslog stream.

Proposed meeting agenda for Fri 09/17 10:00am PT (30m):
1) Walk annotated diagram (Priyom) — 10m
2) Confirm mgmt CIDR and NAT approach (ACME) — 7m
3) Observability endpoint + cert exchange (Neha) — 7m
4) Ops runbook & preflight checklist ownership (Priya/Jonas) — 6m

I'll send the invite and include a short screen-share doc. Please flag anything missing.

Jonas Weber
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Kevin / Marta / ACME infra team — thanks for the rapid review. Per today's prep: 

- ACME confirmed the mgmt /28 (198.51.100.0/28) and RackOps will SNAT control-plane egress to .1-.4 during the cutover window.
- Our checklist now includes explicit listener ports (12000 proxy -> accepts 11211/6379 incoming and maps to internal as needed), mTLS requirement, and a cert exchange step.
- Observability: Neha will coordinate the syslog collector URL and cert exchange (JIRA INFRA-8421).

I've attached the updated runbook and the final annotated diagram for the sync. Please accept the calendar invite for Fri 09/17 10:00am PT — link included in the invite.

Attachments: vpc-coexistence-sketch-v1.pdf (final), ops-handoff-checklist-v1.md (final)
